newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S.-Russia summit to be March 20-21 - Itar-Tass.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Russia summit to be March 20-21 - Itar-Tass.

text.p: The proposed summit between President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin will be held on March 20-21 in Helsinki, Itar-Tass news agency said on Friday.

The agency said it had received the information in a statement from Yeltsin's press service. A Kremlin spokesman declined to confirm the report, saying it had agreed with the United States to distribute details about the summit at nine p.m. (1800 GMT).
Finnish radio in Helsinki said earlier that the meeting would take place on March 19 and 20, possibly continuing to March 21.

In Washington, U.S. officials said the location and date had been agreed during meetings between Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who are conferring as part of a periodic U.S.-Russia liaison effort.
They were to announce the details at a news conference scheduled for 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT), the officials said.

The meeting between Clinton and Yeltsin, originally scheduled to be held in the United States, was relocated to Helsinki to accommodate the Russian president, who is recovering from pneumonia in both lungs.
